sanskrit: सर्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते । अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि सात्त्विकम् ॥
hindiTranslation: जिस ज्ञानके द्वारा साधक सम्पूर्ण विभक्त प्राणियोंमें विभागरहित एक अविनाशी भावसत्ता को देखता है, उस ज्ञानको तुम सात्त्विक समझो ॥
englishTranslation: Know that knowledge to be sattvic by which one sees the one imperishable reality in all beings, undivided among the divided.
essence: True understanding sees one undivided reality inside every divided form.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: Pure understanding sees one unchanging reality in all beings, even though they appear separate.
simpleInsight: Separation stops feeling final. You begin to notice the same reality shining through every face.
detailedMeaning: With Arjuna frozen before battle, Krishna turns from action to vision. He explains that the highest clear understanding sees one imperishable reality in every being, even though they appear divided.
modernRelevance: At a crowded railway station, a porter, a pilgrim and a businessman jostle for the same train. Sattvic knowledge, as Krishna describes it, would see the same imperishable reality in each of the three, under the different clothes and luggage.
translationLiteral: सर्वभूतेषु (in all beings) / येन (by which) / एकम् (one) / भावम् (reality/state) / अव्ययम् (imperishable) / ईक्षते (sees) / अविभक्तम् (undivided) / विभक्तेषु (among the divided) / तत् (that) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / विद्धि (know) / सात्त्विकम् (sattvic)
insight: Sattvic knowledge, Krishna says, sees one imperishable reality within every being, undivided among the divided.

quoteVariants.text: See one imperishable reality in every being. That knowledge is pure.
What looks divided may still be one.
See the one in the many.
